title: requireChannelAuthorIsMember ignores memberKind and nothing notices
description:
MEASURED by scripts/guard-sweep.ts against origin/main afb1dc782, baseline 637 tests / 0 failing.

Mutation: in requireChannelAuthorIsMember (apps/server/src/orchestration/commandInvariants.ts:427), drop the memberKind comparison so the author lookup matches on memberId alone:

  member.memberKind === input.authorRef.memberKind &&
  member.memberId === input.authorRef.memberId,
->
  member.memberId === input.authorRef.memberId,

Result: SURVIVED. All 637 tests in apps/server/src/orchestration stay green.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the impersonation route. A channel whose membership contains a THREAD member whose memberId equals a human's memberId — or the reverse — would resolve that human's post to the thread's membership row, and the event's authorHandle is taken from the row the lookup returns. requireChannelMemberShape refuses those rows on new commands, but it runs on COMMANDS and membership replays from EVENTS, so a row written before it reaches the decider untouched.

The reason no test sees it: every channel fixture gives its members ids that differ in BOTH fields (human/human-walt against thread/thread-pm), so a memberId-only comparison is indistinguishable from the correct one. The separating fixture is one channel with two members sharing a memberId and differing in memberKind.

THIRD INSTANCE OF THIS SHAPE TODAY. The mention-wake reactor's filter (t3_bot-8i2) and the shell stream's membership test (zuy slice b) were the other two, both caught by the same mutation and both fixed by the same kind of fixture.
notes:
Measured on `origin/main` at 82b71b1c5, read-only (`scratchpad/check46h.py`): 65 `(memberKind, memberId)`
pairs across 13 fixture files.

## 46h's premise is no longer true, and that does NOT fix ami

Three files now carry one id under two kinds, so the repository is no longer
uniformly unable to distinguish the two implementations:

| file | the colliding id | kinds |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/server/src/orchestration/decider.issuer.test.ts` | `"thread-boss1"` | human, thread |
| `apps/server/src/persistence/Layers/ProjectionChannels.test.ts` | `"kind-collide"` | human, thread |
| `apps/server/src/server.test.ts` | `HUMAN_OPERATOR_MEMBER_ID` | human, thread |

The last two are #20's — `kind-collide` for `listChannelsForMember`'s SQL and the `server.test.ts`
pair for `rowHasMember`. So #20 closed 46h for the two sites it touched.

## Why the sweep survivor is still real

`author-membership-matches-id-only` SURVIVED on all three bases this morning, and now I know why the
existing collision does not kill it. `decider.issuer.test.ts`'s human-with-a-thread-id fixtures
(lines 497-498 and 522) are consumed by a **different guard**: both tests assert
`error.detail` contains `"is a thread id"`, i.e. the member-SHAPE invariant refuses that member
before `requireChannelAuthorIsMember` is ever reached. The collision is spent proving the shape
guard, so it cannot also prove the membership guard.

**So ami's fixture has to thread a needle:** a member whose `memberId` equals the author ref's and
whose `memberKind` differs, which the member-shape guard ADMITS. The naive fixture — a `human`
member carrying a thread-shaped id — is refused earlier and tests nothing about membership. Before
writing it, establish what `requireCanonicalChannelMember` treats as "a thread id", and pick an id
that is legal for both kinds.

`requireChannelAuthorIsMember` itself is CORRECT on main — `commandInvariants.ts:432-436` compares
`memberKind` AND `memberId`. ami is an unpinned guard, not a wrong one, so its fix is a test and a
fixture, not a change to the guard. Prove it with the named mutant: drop the `memberKind` clause and
the new test must go red and be the only one that does.

Not started — the PM's order is #19 lanes, #17 lanes, then ami.

title: Gateway CreatePostInput.authorRef is stale: a44 removed authorRef from channel.post.create and the live-layer wiring instruction still points at it
description:
Found by the QA lane on PR #6 (t3_bot-a44), executed against both branches, and it spans the two PRs so neither side's tests can see it.

WHAT IS STALE. On origin/boss3/t3_bot-2x5-canonical-names (PR #5), channelGateway.ts:108-120 declares CreatePostInput.authorRef, and its docstring instructs whoever wires the live layer: "The live layer translates this to the `authorRef` its command carries." handlers.ts:250 builds that field: authorRef: { memberKind: "thread", memberId: input.threadId }.

PR #6 REMOVES authorRef from channel.post.create entirely. The decider derives the author from an engine-stamped issuer on the envelope instead, because the command carrying its own author is what made authorship forgeable (SEC-1). There is no field for the live layer to translate authorRef INTO.

WHY IT BITES AFTER BOTH MERGE. PR #5 merges first, PR #6 second. So on the resulting main the only instruction in the repo for wiring the live ChannelGateway points at a command field that does not exist. Worse than a stale comment: a gateway that follows it dispatches without an issuer, and channel commands now FAIL CLOSED without one — so every agent post is refused with "arrived without an issuer and cannot be authorized". The person wiring 0uq gets a correct-looking implementation that refuses everything.

This is the Factory-to-Component Wiring Rule in the project CLAUDE.md: a44 changed what the dispatch call site must pass, and the instruction for the call site that does not exist yet was not updated with it.

WHAT THE CORRECT WIRING IS, so this is actionable rather than just a warning:
  engine.dispatch(command, { issuer: { memberKind: "thread", memberId: <the credential's threadId> } })
The toolkit's threadId is exactly the right value — it comes from the MCP credential, which is the whole point of the issuer. CreatePostInput.authorRef can then be dropped from the gateway shape, since the gateway no longer needs to carry an author at all.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. channelGateway.ts's CreatePostInput no longer declares authorRef, or its docstring names `issuer` and the dispatch option instead of a command field.
2. handlers.ts no longer builds an authorRef for the post path.
3. A test that the live wiring supplies an issuer — the end-to-end probe on a44's criterion 1, which is what 0uq owes: an MCP-credentialed call posting with any spoofed author lands with authorHandle = the credential's thread.

BLOCKS t3_bot-0uq: whoever implements the live gateway is the person this misleads.
notes:
ALL THREE CRITERIA DONE in PR #13 (t3_bot-0uq).

1. CreatePostInput no longer declares authorRef; it carries the calling thread, and the docstring shows the DISPATCH OPTION rather than describing a field - because the mistake this bead prevents is a TRANSLATION, and you cannot prevent a translation by describing the destination.
2. handlers.ts builds threadId. The gateway's own ChannelAuthorRef declaration is deleted; the contracts type of that name is the decider's and stays.
3. THE PROBE, which was the criterion that needed the live layer: commsLive.integration.test.ts drives the real handlers through ChannelGatewayLive onto a real engine and asserts what the aggregate STORED. An agent calls with the arguments it chose; the author that lands is the credential's thread.

Two mutations pin it, both red: dispatch with NO issuer (which is precisely the defect this bead describes - a correct-looking gateway that refuses every post), and issue as a DIFFERENT thread.

That second mutant is the one worth noting. Criterion 3 says 'any spoofed author lands with authorHandle = the credential's thread'. There is no longer any way to spoof an author - the command has no such field - so the spoofing half of the criterion is unreachable by construction, and what the test pins instead is the property that replaced it: the issuer is the credential's thread and nothing else.

Closes when #13 merges.

title: Agents-only channel cannot be un-latched by posting once the wake budget is exhausted
description:
`t3_bot-64d` stops waking in a channel once its budget is spent, and the way out is a HUMAN member's
post. In a channel with no human member there is no such post to make: the decider refuses a post from
a non-member (`requireChannelAuthorIsMember`), so an operator cannot simply type into it.

MEASURED by #23's security lane, not reasoned: the operator's reset post is refused with "not a member"
and the channel stays latched.

NOT REACHABLE IN M1, which is why this is P3 rather than a blocker: the seeder puts walt in every
seeded channel, so every channel that exists today has a human member. It becomes reachable the moment
a channel is created without one — which nothing forbids, and which an agent creating its own working
channel would do by default.

MITIGATED, NOT FIXED, in #23: the ERROR line now names the recovery rather than only the condition —
"A HUMAN member's post clears it; if none is a member, add yourself (channel.member.add) and then
post." That turns an unactionable message into two steps, and it is deliberately all that PR does. PM
ruled NO new mechanism for M1.

THE REAL FIX IS A CHOICE, and it should be made once rather than drifted into:
  (a) refuse `channel.create` without at least one human member — cheap, and arguably wrong: an
      agents-only channel is a legitimate thing to want.
  (b) let the latch expire after a long fixed period (an hour, a day) as a backstop, keeping the human
      post as the fast path. Reintroduces the refill this bead's parent deliberately removed, so the
      period has to be long enough that a runaway is not worth resuming.
  (c) surface the latched state somewhere a human LOOKS — the channel list, a badge — so the recovery
      is discoverable without reading a server log. This is the only option that helps the
      single-operator case too, where the human is a member and simply has not noticed.

(c) is the one I would argue for, and it wants the channel UI that `t3_bot-zuy` built, so it is
naturally post-M1.

DO NOT CLOSE THIS by weakening the membership check on posts. That check is `t3_bot-a44`'s, it is what
stops any caller posting as anyone, and it is load-bearing.

Filed by boss3 out of #23's security lane (SEC-23-02).

title: Socket RPC errors put the full internal cause chain on the wire
description:
SEC-25-01 on PR 25, generalised. About twenty RPC error classes in apps/server/src/ws.ts attach cause: Schema.optional(Schema.Defect()), which serialises the entire nested chain to the client.

MEASURED by #25's security lane, encoding the real value: {_tag: OrchestrationReadChannelPostsError, message: ..., cause: {name: PersistenceSqlError, message: 'SQL error in ProjectionChannelRepository.listPostsBackward:query: no such column: projection_channel_posts.sequence', cause: {name: Error, message: 'SQLITE_ERROR: near "sequenc": syntax error (/Users/walt/.t3/userdata/state.sqlite)'}}} — 381 bytes including internal schema and a filesystem path.

The recipient is any authenticated client holding only AuthOrchestrationReadScope, which on this product can be a remote paired browser or the mobile app over T3 Connect rather than the operator at the keyboard. Nothing secret and no corruption, which is why the lane rated it impact 2 / LOW.

The HTTP side already does the opposite: failEnvironmentInternal logs the cause server-side and returns {code, reason, traceId} (apps/server/src/auth/http.ts:160-172). title: No test reaches OrchestrationCommandIdConflictError through the production dispatch path
description:
Found by the test-coverage lane during /review-pr on PR #3 (t3_bot-eas), and left out of that PR deliberately: the gap predates it and the PR does not widen it.

commandToAggregateRef's output is compared against a stored command receipt's aggregate to decide whether a replayed commandId is a genuine retry or a collision, raising OrchestrationCommandIdConflictError (OrchestrationEngine.ts:219-231). That comparison is the ONE production behaviour the routing result gates.

EXECUTED by the lane: `rg -n "OrchestrationCommandIdConflictError" apps packages -g '*.ts'` returns 7 hits, all in Errors.ts and OrchestrationEngine.ts. Zero in any test file. Nothing exercises the conflict path.

Why it matters more than it looks: the ACCEPTED receipt is stamped from the decider's event (OrchestrationEngine.ts:366) while the conflict check compares the ROUTER's answer (:221). If those two mappings disagree, a legitimate replay of a command that already succeeded is refused. PR #3 now asserts the two mappings agree for every declared command, which closes the divergence at the unit level — but nothing drives the conflict path itself through the production dispatch entry point.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (written so the wrong fix fails):
1. The test MUST dispatch through the real engine (createOrchestrationSystem in OrchestrationEngine.test.ts), not call commandToAggregateRef or the receipt repository directly. A unit test of the comparison does not verify the assembled path and does not close this.
2. It MUST assert the error carries BOTH aggregate scopes — the receipt's and the command's — not merely that an OrchestrationCommandIdConflictError was raised. Every conflict produces the same tag, so a tag-only assertion is non-discriminating (boss1 hit exactly this with five channel rejection tests that all passed against a synthesised requireChannel).
3. It MUST go RED when the routing switch is mutated so a command's aggregate disagrees with the decider's. If the test passes with that mutation applied, it is not testing the conflict this bead is about.
4. State whether a replay that SHOULD succeed (same commandId, same aggregate) still succeeds. A fix that makes every replay conflict would satisfy 1-3 and be worse than the gap.

Not M1-blocking. Nothing in the channel work depends on it.

title: Branding a type retroactively turns every unguarded .make on outside input into a defect site, and .pipe guards do not cover it
description:
Found on PR #13 as one instance; filed as the CLASS because the instance was cheap and the class is not.

WHAT HAPPENED ONCE. `t3_bot-2d2` merged mid-review and gave `ChannelId`/`ChannelPostId` a pattern check. `Schema.brand(...).make` THROWS on a value the check refuses. `channelGatewayLive.getPost` had:

    channels.getPost({ channelId: ChannelId.make(channelId), postId: ChannelPostId.make(postId) })
      .pipe(Effect.map(...), Effect.mapError(...))

and the caller in `handlers.ts` wrapped THAT with `.pipe(Effect.catchTags(...), Effect.catchCause(writeDefect))`. None of it ran. The throw happens while `channels.getPost(...)` is being CALLED — during argument evaluation — so no Effect has been constructed yet and nothing has been piped. `writeDefect` exists for exactly this and never saw it.

`parentPostId` is agent-supplied and `tools.ts` checked only `isNonEmpty()`, so `comms_reply` with "a:b", "has space", "   ", "post-<emoji>" or a 65-character id all died. What reached the agent was the raw Effect `SchemaIssue` AST including the regex source — worse than a wrong tag.

WHY IT IS A CLASS AND NOT A LINE.

1. The defect is created by a change to a DIFFERENT package. `packages/contracts` tightened a brand; `apps/server`'s call sites did not change and did not need to compile differently. Every `.make` that was total became partial, silently, and TypeScript cannot see it — `.make` returns the branded type either way.
2. The guard that looks like it covers it does not. A reviewer reading `getPost(...).pipe(Effect.catchCause(writeDefect))` sees a guarded call. The guard applies to the Effect, and the throw precedes the Effect.
3. Tests do not catch it, because a test that drives the path with a WELL-FORMED id exercises the same line successfully. #13 had 870 green tests over this bug; the only thing that found it was driving the path with a malformed id, which nothing did.

WHERE TO LOOK. Any `X.make(v)` where `X` is a branded schema carrying a check and `v` came from outside the server — a tool argument, an RPC payload, a URL segment, a header, a database row written under an older rule. Especially inside an argument list, where the guard cannot reach it. `ThreadId`, `ProjectId`, `EnvironmentId`, `CommandId`, `MessageId`, `ChannelMemberHandle` are `TrimmedNonEmptyString` today and so throw only on empty/whitespace; `ChannelId` and `ChannelPostId` carry the opaque-id pattern and throw on much more. The first group is one bead away from joining the second, and that is the day this bites everywhere at once.

IMMINENT: `t3_bot-zuy` puts channel ids and post ids on the wire from a browser. A client-supplied channelId reaching `ChannelId.make` is the same defect with a different caller. boss1 has been told; this bead is so it is not only in a board message.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Enumerate every `.make` on a branded-with-check schema in `apps/server` reached from outside input, and say for each whether it is guarded, unreachable, or fixed. A list with "probably fine" entries does not satisfy this.
2. Each one that is agent- or client-reachable is driven by a test with a value the brand REFUSES, asserting a typed failure and not a defect. A test with a well-formed value does not count — it passes either way.
3. State the rule in one place a reader will find: decode (`Schema.decodeUnknownOption` / `decodeUnknownEither`) for outside input, `.make` only for values the server itself constructed or has already validated.
4. Consider a lint rule for `.make(` inside a call's argument list. Optional, but say yes or no with a reason rather than leaving it unasked.

FIXED IN #13 for the one reachable instance: `getPost` decodes through the brand and treats a refusal as absence, so an id the type cannot hold reads as "no such post" — true, and actionable by the agent.
notes:
PR #13 CLOSED ITS THREE REACHABLE INSTANCES RATHER THAN LEAVING ANY ANNOTATED, on a blind verifier's argument I initially resisted: what a comment records here is a live CONTRACT VIOLATION, not a TODO. createPost declares five typed failures and delivered a raw schema Die with a serialised AST; the next caller writes an exhaustive catchTags, looks correct, and is wrong. And a third coupling annotated 'this is the coupling we do not rely on', in a change that removed two others, makes the rule read as optional.

FOUR SITES IN #13, all now total:
  getPost's ChannelPostId.make      -> decoded through the brand, refusal reads as absence
  readPosts' requireSequence        -> Effect.suspend (the guard written AGAINST this class was an instance of it)
  getPost's ChannelId.make          -> Effect.suspend
  createPost's ChannelPostId.make   -> decoded, refused as ChannelWriteConflict(retryable:false)

THE ASSERTION THAT DISTINGUISHES THIS CLASS is Effect.exit, and it is the reusable part. A throw at CALL time fails a test uncatchably; a defect inside the Effect yields a Failure VALUE. Both fail a test, and the summary line looks identical - so an assertion that only checks THAT the call failed measures nothing. Effect.exit can only produce a Failure value if the Effect was built at all. Effect.flip cannot be used: it propagates a die rather than yielding it.

AND A MUTATION WARNING for whoever does criterion 1: reverting the USE of a decoded value to .make while leaving the decode in place leaves tests green, because the decode still fails first. That reads as a surviving mutant and is an incomplete mutation. Remove the decode AND restore the .make.

title: One 'Earlier posts' click kills live arrival for good; nothing returns the region to the newest page
description:
The live-arrival effect is gated on `cursor === undefined`, and `setCursor` is called at exactly ONE site (the 'Earlier posts' button), always with a non-undefined cursor. There is no scroll handler, no jump-to-latest control, and sending a post does not reset it — so after one click the region never re-reads for the rest of the instance's life. On the 58-post #seniors fixture that is one click.

The comment above the effect says 'the next return to the bottom picks it up'. There is no return to the bottom in the code; the comment describes a path that does not exist, which this repo treats as a defect in its own right.

title: ChannelGateway.createPost declares three failures no live implementation can produce; the decider's refusals are only tellable apart by prose
description:
`ChannelGatewayShape.createPost` declares five failures. `ChannelGatewayLive` can produce two: `ChannelStoreUnavailable` and `ChannelWriteConflict`. The other three — `ChannelMembershipRevoked`, `ChannelMentionUnresolvable`, `ChannelArchived` — are constructed only by test fakes. Verified on PR #13 by blind triage:

    rg -n 'new ChannelMembershipRevoked|new ChannelMentionUnresolvable' apps packages --type ts
    commsSeam.integration.test.ts:150 · handlers.test.ts:697 · handlers.test.ts:711

Three hits, all fakes. No production construction site. `ChannelArchived` joined them in #13 when the archived decision moved to the caller, which is where it belongs (it is decided from the channel the caller already proved membership on).

WHY THE LIVE LAYER CANNOT PRODUCE THEM. The decider's refusals all arrive as one `OrchestrationCommandInvariantError` whose only distinguishing feature is its `detail` string: "Author is not a member of channel 'x'.", "Mentions do not resolve to members of channel 'x': ghost." Telling them apart means matching on that prose, which is the thing the seam's own comment says not to do — and #13 stopped forwarding that prose to agents at all, because it leaks the internal channelId.

WHAT THIS COSTS TODAY. `CommsMembershipLostError` — the best-worded error in the toolkit, which tells an agent its membership was revoked between the check and the write — is production-dead. A revoked membership reaches the agent as a generic "the channel refused the post", correctly marked non-retryable but unexplained. A second caller of this seam (the web UI, t3_bot-zuy slice b) would read the declared union and write handling for three cases that never arrive.

DECIDED ON #13, and recorded here so the next reader does not re-litigate it: the tags STAY, documented as having no live producer, rather than being deleted. Deleting them is smaller and honest but throws away the vocabulary just as a second caller arrives, and the right fix is to make the distinctions real rather than to stop declaring them.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. `OrchestrationCommandInvariantError` carries a machine-readable reason (a tagged member or a `reason` literal), set where each invariant fails in `commandInvariants.ts` — not derived from the message.
2. `ChannelGatewayLive` maps at least the membership and mention-resolution refusals to their seam errors from that field, with no string matching anywhere in the path.
3. `CommsMembershipLostError` is produced through the LIVE gateway in a test, not a fake: remove the member with a real `channel.member.remove` dispatch between the toolkit's check and the write.
4. The gateway's declared failure union contains no member that no implementation can produce — assert it, or state per member which implementation produces it.
5. No agent-visible string carries the internal channelId or the phrase "Orchestration command invariant failed". #13 closed this; it must stay closed.

Touches `apps/server/src/orchestration/*` (shared — CLAIM on the board first).

title: The comms toolkit's agent-facing errors apply a good convention unevenly
description:
Six findings from the design lane on PR #10, all triaged DEFERRED - none is this PR's doing, and together they are one coherent piece of work rather than six edits.

THE FAILURE MODE THEY SHARE is the one this area has already produced once: an error that routes the agent back to the tool that produced the problem. CommsMemberNotFoundError points at comms_read_channel, which is the right pointer when the handle was mistyped and an infinite retry when the member list is what is wrong - the legacy-row case documented as terminal in docs/internals/channel-identity.md.

THE SIX:
1. The one error that discards a WHOLE POST is the only post-path error that does not say so. An agent that reads 'member not found' and retries without the bad mention has guessed right; one that retries the same post has lost the message and does not know.
2. A raw Effect cause dump is interpolated into an error an agent reads, on both the post and the read paths.
3. 'Try again.' is issued without stating whether the first attempt landed, in a toolkit that documents retries as duplicating.
4. The 'consult comms_read_channel' pointer sits on the error where it can loop and is missing from the error where it would work.
5. A channel name that is only sigils or whitespace produces an error naming the empty string.
6. The terminal legacy-row case has no distinct error at all - it arrives as member-not-found.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING AS ONE THING: these errors are an INTERFACE, and the reader is an agent that will act on the text. The convention the toolkit already has is good - conflate 'no such channel' with 'you are not a member', name every bad handle at once, tell the agent what to do next. It is applied unevenly, and the unevenness is what produces loops.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. Every comms error states whether the operation LANDED, since that decides whether a retry duplicates.
2. No error interpolates an internal cause. Log it; do not hand it to an agent.
3. An error that points the agent at a tool must be reachable only when that tool can fix the problem.
4. A test per error asserting the agent-visible text, not the tag - the tag is not what an agent reads.
5. Decide, once, whether the legacy-row refusal deserves its own error, and say why either way.

title: ChannelMember.handle's contract docstring specifies the reverted rule
description:
Named independently by FIVE review lanes on PR #10 (security, quality, history, contracts, design) and triaged DEFERRED - false since PR #5's revert rather than since #10, so a bead rather than an edit in that PR.

WHERE. apps/server/src/mcp/toolkits/comms/channelGateway.ts, ChannelMember.handle. It says the handle is 'Trimmed and non-empty, and nothing more: unlike a channel name this is NOT case-folded, because the aggregate matches it byte-exactly', and names t3_bot-iin as the condition for that changing. iin has landed. The aggregate canonicalises every handle on every path that stores or compares one.

WHY IT IS P1 DESPITE BEING A COMMENT. It is the SPECIFICATION whoever writes the live gateway layer reads, and that is t3_bot-0uq, which is next. A gateway built to this docstring emits handles under the reverted rule and reproduces the PR #5 regression: the whole post refused for one mention, with the error telling the agent to consult the tool that produced the handle.

WHAT IT SHOULD SAY. Canonical, by the shared rule with '@' as the sigil, applied by the aggregate. A caller may fold and strip to FIND a member; what it EMITS must be the stored bytes, because the aggregate resolves a mention with an exact comparison and the read model can hold a row written under an older form of the rule.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. The docstring states the rule that holds, including the emit half - matching is forgiving, delivery is not.
2. It does not name a bead as its expiry condition. That is what let it rot: the condition was met and nothing pointed back at the text.
3. Check the file for other statements of the old rule while there; the lanes named this one, and the module header's 'Ids are string here' paragraph should be re-read against t3_bot-2d2 now that ids are branded patterns.
4. Blocks 0uq.
notes:
DONE in PR #13 (t3_bot-0uq) as its first commit, per pm 040235: the specification is rewritten BEFORE the gateway is built to it, because the gateway is built by reading it.

ChannelMember.handle now states the rule that holds - canonical by the shared rule with @ as the sigil, applied by the aggregate on every path that stores or compares a handle - AND the half that keeps burning this area: matching is forgiving, delivery is not. A caller may fold to FIND a member; what it EMITS must be the stored bytes, because the read model can hold a row written under an older form of the rule.

The criterion that mattered most is honoured: it does NOT name a bead as its expiry condition. That is what let the original rot - iin landed, the condition was met, and nothing pointed back at the text. Five review lanes had to find it.

Closes when #13 merges.

title: comms cursor is a global event sequence, so a cursor earned in one channel silently reads as caught-up in another
description:
The non-numeric half is fixed in PR #13: `comms_read_channel`'s `cursor` is checked against `^[0-9]+$` at the tool schema, and `ChannelGatewayLive` dies rather than coercing. This bead is the half that fix does NOT close.

WHAT IS STILL WRONG. `nextCursor` is `String(row.sequence)` — the GLOBAL orchestration event sequence, not a per-channel offset. It is well-formed digits, so it passes the new schema check, and `afterSequence` in another channel simply matches no row. Measured during PR #13's review, through the real tool on the live gateway:

    X alpha page1: ["alpha-0","alpha-1"]  cursor: "9"
    X bravo with alpha's cursor: []  next: null
    X bravo plain: ["bravo-0","bravo-1","bravo-2"]

Three unread posts in #bravo behind a successful reply whose wire shape is byte-for-byte "you are caught up". An agent cannot detect it: it stops reading that channel.

WHY IT IS A REAL PATH, not a contrived one. An agent holding cursors for several channels has no type-level reason to keep them apart — `nextCursor` is a bare `Schema.String` in `ReadChannelResult` with no channel in it, and the tool description says only "pass as cursor to read the posts after this page". The mistake is invisible on both sides.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
1. A cursor issued for one channel, presented to another, does NOT return an empty page. Either it is refused with an agent-readable error naming the mismatch, or the cursor is per-channel and the foreign value cannot parse.
2. A test posts to two channels, pages the first, then presents that cursor to the second and asserts the refusal — with the second channel's posts asserted present by a plain read in the same test, so the assertion cannot pass by the channel being empty.
3. Whatever shape is chosen, the cursor stays opaque to the agent: it is handed back verbatim and never constructed by the caller.
4. State what happens to a cursor issued before this change. They are not persisted anywhere — an agent holds one for the length of a conversation — so the answer may be "nothing", but say it rather than leave it.

SHAPE, not binding: `${channelId}:${sequence}` makes the cursor self-describing and the mismatch detectable. Note that `ChannelId` is now `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}$` (t3_bot-2d2, merged), so a colon cannot occur inside the id and the split is unambiguous — which was NOT true when the reactor's wake key hit exactly this collision and had to escape both halves.

Found by the contracts and security lanes on PR #13, confirmed by blind triage with the probe above.

ALL TRIAGE FIXES DONE at 54066bb95 on base 852baba35. Gate re-run: vp check 0, vpr typecheck 0, apps/server 4655 passed / 12 failed - the same twelve environment failures by NAME as the baseline worktree. Blind verification dispatched.

  1. The nominal ChannelMemberRef (class with a private field) MOVES to a leaf module in packages/contracts, so both persistence and the mcp toolkit can import it. It currently lives in the toolkit's seam, which is the wrong home once persistence needs it.
  2. DELETE boss1's HUMAN_OPERATOR_CHANNEL_MEMBER and replace every use with refFromOperatorSession(), so there is exactly one way to obtain the operator's ref. Two constants for one identity is how the divergence that produced the #14 two-door defect began.
  3. ABSORB boss1's listChannelsForMember and getChannelWithActivityById as they landed in #20 - re-type them onto the seam, do NOT re-implement. I had deferred listChannelsForMember out of this PR precisely because writing a second copy would collide with his; the ruling makes that deferral permanent and turns it into an absorb.

Order is #20 then #18, so none of the above can start until #20 is merged.

WHY THE DEFERRAL WAS RIGHT AND IS NOW RECORDED: writing my own listChannelsForMember would have produced two implementations of one read, which is the defect class this repo has been burned by four times (canonicaliser, cursor shape, member comparison, operator identity). The cost of waiting is one rebase; the cost of duplicating is a divergence nobody sees until the two disagree.

title: Table-driven test: assert every command type routes to its expected aggregate
description:
Found by the QA lane during /review-pr on PR #2 (t3_bot-l8i), mutation E; verified at source by boss1.

commandToAggregateRef uses 'command satisfies never' in its default branch. That proves EXHAUSTIVENESS (every command has some branch). It proves NOTHING about CORRECTNESS (that each command sits in the RIGHT branch).

Demonstrated: moving case 'thread.pull-request.sync' from the thread branch into the project branch gives server typecheck exit 0 / zero errors, engine test 29/29 pass, ThreadPullRequestReactor 13/13 pass. Fully GREEN. Cause: ThreadPullRequestSyncCommand (packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts:1454-1459) carries BOTH threadId AND projectId, so command.projectId resolves in the project branch and the command is silently stamped aggregateKind 'project'.

Contrast: mutation D moved 'thread.create' (no projectId) into the project branch - tests went RED but typecheck was STILL exit 0. So even where something catches it, it is the suite, not the compiler.

Blast radius if it happens: a thread's events, command receipt, and hasEventAfter scope attach to a project aggregate. Same damage class as the original silent-misroute this PR set out to prevent.

Scope of the fix: a table-driven test over the OrchestrationCommand union asserting each command type maps to its expected aggregateKind/aggregateId. Needs commandToAggregateRef exported (currently module-local at apps/server/src/orchestration/Layers/OrchestrationEngine.ts:73) or exercised through dispatch.

Deliberately NOT done in PR #2: it is new work, not a line-edit, and widening a 111-line PR to chase it is scope creep. The 39 hand-maintained case labels make this MORE valuable over time, not less - every added command is another chance to put a case in the wrong group.

title: Scroll-triggered paging for the channel post region
description:
HIST-25-05 on PR 25. The region pages with a control rather than a scroll handler, and the deferral was parked on t3_bot-ajw — the bead PR 25 CLOSES, so the refinement would have gone with it. This bead carries it instead, with a dep on ajw.

The obstacle is render timing, not a missing capability, and the earlier comment said the wrong thing about it (QUAL-25-03): page.waiting IS in-flight state the atom exposes and this component already reads it twice. But it is state, so it changes on re-render, and every scroll event inside one frame reads the value from before the dispatch. A scroll guard needs a ref that flips synchronously where the fetch is dispatched — three lines. A scroll-triggered fetch otherwise fires repeatedly while the momentum of one flick carries the container past the threshold.

title: Non-member and missing channel are indistinguishable only by convention, not by test
description:
Raised by boss1's 22:30 finding on the mention-error ordering leak (2b6d71ba0), checked against the comms toolkit, and it is the same family one step removed.

THE PROPERTY: a caller must not be able to tell "this channel does not exist" from "this channel exists and I am not in it". Both must produce the identical CommsChannelNotFoundError. Otherwise any agent holding a comms credential can enumerate private channel names by probing.

TODAY IT HOLDS STRUCTURALLY, which is stronger than boss1's case: membership is a PARAMETER of the lookup (channels.getChannelForMember(name, scope.threadId), handlers.ts:138), not a guard that runs after it, so a non-member gets Option.none and falls into the SAME single branch as a missing channel (handlers.ts:143-145). There is no ordering to swap. That is the design and it should be preserved deliberately rather than by accident.

THE GAP: handlers.test.ts:242 pins only the NON-MEMBER side. Its comment says "Same error a missing channel gives" and then hardcodes what it believes that error to be. Nothing drives a channel that simply does not exist and compares. So the divergence is reachable from the other direction: change the MISSING-channel branch - add a reason field, a distinct tag, a different channel value - and the non-member test stays green while the two errors become distinguishable. The security property is asserted in a comment and checked on one side.

This becomes live rather than theoretical when the gateway gains a typed "exists but not a member" result, which is a natural thing to want for auditing. At that point mapping it to its own tool error is the obvious change and nothing stops it.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (written so the wrong fix fails):
1. The test MUST drive BOTH cases through the real handler in one test and assert the two errors are equal to each other - not each equal to a hardcoded literal. Two tests that each pin their own expected shape do not pin the relationship; that is the current state and it is what lets the two drift apart.
2. The comparison MUST be over the whole error value, not a _tag match. Every distinguishable variant this is guarding against shares the tag; a toMatchObject with only _tag passes against the exact leak it is supposed to prevent.
3. It MUST go RED when the missing-channel branch is mutated to carry any distinguishing field. Apply that mutation and record the output in the PR.
4. State whether a member asking for a channel that DOES exist still gets it. A fix that collapses every lookup to not-found would satisfy 1-3 and break the toolkit.

Not M1-blocking. The property holds today; this pins it so it keeps holding.
notes:
CRITERION 1 CLOSED FOR THE LIVE PATH in PR #13 (643d4149b), which is the path an enumeration attack would actually run against. Criteria 2, 3 and 4 are satisfied for that path too; the bead stays open for the SEAM tests, which still pin one side each.

WHAT LANDED: commsLive.integration.test.ts drives BOTH cases through the real handler in one test - a channel the caller was removed from, and a channel that does not exist - and asserts the two error values are equal TO EACH OTHER. The names necessarily differ, because each error echoes what the CALLER asked for, so equality is asserted after substituting each request's own name out of the serialised error. That is what isolates the property: nothing in the answer varies with what is STORED.

Criterion 2 (whole value, not a _tag match): satisfied - the comparison is over the JSON-serialised error, every field.
Criterion 3 (RED on a distinguishing field): measured. Making the missing-channel branch fail with a store error instead of Option.none reds it, 1 failed / 66 passed.
Criterion 4 (a member asking for a channel that DOES exist still gets it): covered by 'reads back what the other agent posted, through the same tools' in the same file.

STILL OPEN, and why: commsSeam.integration.test.ts:422 and :429 remain one-sided pins against hardcoded literals. They test the FAKE gateway's conflation, which is a different implementation of the same property, and #13 did not touch them.

AND THE RATIONALE IN THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION IS STALE - see the note above it. It says the property holds structurally because membership is a parameter of the lookup. That was true of the seam and is false of ChannelGatewayLive, where the lookup runs first and membership is a guard after it. The structural argument is no longer a reason to leave this at P3; the new test is.

title: Move hierarchy.seed above reactors.start so a wake cannot race the instance repair
description:
bug30's BUG-30-01 on PR #30 (medium severity, medium confidence — read from the startup ordering, NOT executed).

MEASURED by reading apps/server/src/serverRuntimeStartup.ts: "reactors.start" is a startup phase at :894 and "hierarchy.seed" is one at :916, so the reactors are already draining when the seed runs. Nothing between them depends on the seed.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: PR #30 added an instance repair inside seedHierarchy — the first seed step whose correctness depends on landing BEFORE a reactor reads the row it fixes. The harmful interleaving: a booted environment holds an un-consumed channel post mentioning a seeded thread (a wake dispatch that failed transiently, or a post written just before the process died, so the channel's wake cursor never advanced past it). On the next boot MentionWakeReactor drains the post and dispatches thread.turn.start against a thread whose modelSelection is still 'claude'; ProviderCommandReactor resolves the instance at drain time (ensureSessionForThread) and fails with "references unknown provider instance 'claude'" — and MentionWakeReactor advances its cursor on a successful DISPATCH, not on a successful turn (its own comment). So that one post is consumed with no answer, on the boot whose job was to make the answer possible. Every later post is fine, because the repair has landed by then.

NOT CLOSED BY THE COMMAND GATE. I checked: only ws.ts uses commandGate.enqueueCommand (plus the HTTP readiness layer). Reactors do not go through it, and the failing step is a provider call rather than a dispatch, so the gate would not stop it either way.

THE FIX: move the hierarchy.seed phase above reactors.start. It has no dependency on the reactors — the seeder calls engine.dispatch directly and awaits no reactor receipt — and the phase's existing comment only constrains it to precede the autoBootstrap fork.

WHY IT IS A SEPARATE BEAD: it is a boot-ordering change whose effect cannot be shown by the test suite, and neither bug30 nor I could execute the race (it needs the whole server layer, and the ground rules forbid starting a dev server for it). Reordering a startup phase on an unexecuted argument, inside a PR about a seeded thread's instance id, is two concerns. PR #30 states the accepted interleaving in a comment at the seed phase and points here.

ACCEPTANCE: either the phase moves and something demonstrates the ordering (a startup-phase-order assertion is cheap and would have caught this class), or the interleaving is accepted in writing with the reason.

title: Canonicalise member handles in the aggregate, then restore the toolkit fold
description:
Found by three independent /review-pr lanes on PR #5 (security, bug-hunter, contracts), each executing rather than reading, and confirmed at source before acting.

THE RULE SAYS HANDLES FOLD CASE. NOTHING IMPLEMENTS IT. The pm's 2026-09-11 22:39 ruling says "Handles: same rule" as channel names. On origin/boss1/t3_bot-yyd-channel-decider that is true for names and false for handles:

  - ChannelMemberHandle = makeEntityId("ChannelMemberHandle") -> branded TrimmedNonEmptyString (baseSchemas.ts:117, 104-106). Trimmed only; "Boss1" and "boss1" are both valid.
  - canonicalChannelName has exactly two call sites, decider.ts:2039 and :2060, both on command.name. channel.create passes command.members through verbatim (:2040); channel.member.add passes command.member verbatim (:2120).
  - requireChannelHandlesUnique compares with an exact Set (commandInvariants.ts:105-122), so "Boss1" and "boss1" are two legal, distinct members of one channel.
  - requireChannelMentionsResolve compares new Set(members.map(m => m.handle)) with exact has() (commandInvariants.ts:157-158).
  - projection_channel_members is PRIMARY KEY (channel_id, handle) with no COLLATE (051_ProjectionChannels.ts:41). projection_channels.name carries an "always stored canonical" comment; the members table carries no such comment because no such thing is true.

WHAT THAT COST, AND IT WAS A REGRESSION I SHIPPED. PR #5 folded case in normalizeHandle on the strength of the ruling. Executed end-to-end against the real requireChannelMentionsResolve by the security lane, member stored as "Boss1":

  1. comms_read_channel("seniors")               -> members: ["boss1", "boss3"]
  2. comms_post(mentions: ["boss1"])             -> toolkit emits "boss1"
  3. requireChannelMentionsResolve               -> handles = {"Boss1"}; "boss1" absent
  4. whole post REJECTED as an unresolvable mention
  5. agent sees: "Not members of this channel: boss1. Use comms_read_channel to see who is."

The tool it is told to consult is the tool that produced the wrong handle. An unrecoverable loop, and byte-exact handles worked before the change.

DONE IN PR #5, NOT THE FIX: the fold was reverted, the gateway's handle docstring narrowed to what ChannelMemberHandle actually guarantees, and a test pins byte-exact passthrough so re-adding the fold turns it red (verified: "expected [ 'boss1' ] to deeply equal [ 'Boss1' ]"). Channel NAMES still fold; that half is fully backed by the decider.

THE FIX, and it has to land as ONE change across both halves:
1. canonicalChannelHandle beside canonicalChannelName in commandInvariants.ts, same shape (trim, strip leading @, trim, lowercase).
2. Applied in the decider at channel.create (every member), channel.member.add (member), channel.member.remove (handle), and channel.post.create (mentions).
3. requireChannelHandlesUnique compares canonical handles, so "Boss1" and "boss1" can no longer both be members.
4. THEN restore .toLowerCase() in the toolkit's normalizeHandle and widen the gateway docstring back.

Order matters: the toolkit half alone is the regression above. The decider half alone is harmless.

MIGRATION QUESTION THAT MUST BE ANSWERED, not assumed: existing rows. Any channel already carrying "Boss1" keeps it, and canonicalising only new writes leaves the same mismatch for old members. Either a migration folds projection_channel_members.handle in place - which can COLLIDE, since (channel_id,"Boss1") and (channel_id,"boss1") are both legal today and fold to one key - or the rule applies only to channels created after it lands, which must then be stated rather than discovered.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (written so the wrong fix fails):
1. A post mentioning "@Boss1" MUST succeed when the member was created as "Boss1", AND when it was created as "boss1". Both directions, through the real decider invariant, not a fake.
2. Creating a channel with members "Boss1" and "boss1" MUST be rejected by requireChannelHandlesUnique. Without this, canonicalising the mention path alone makes two members collapse onto one wake.
3. comms_read_channel's member list MUST be byte-identical to what a mention needs. Assert equality between the two, not each against a literal - that is the relationship that broke here, and pinning the two sides separately is what let them drift.
4. State what happens to handles stored before the change. A fix that silently leaves them mismatched satisfies 1-3 for new channels and reproduces this bug for every existing one.
5. The toolkit's fold MUST NOT be restored in the same commit as the decider change unless the same test proves both directions of criterion 1 - otherwise a bisect lands on a commit where posting is broken.
notes:
DOC DRAFT v2, superseding the one above. Rewritten after the key/value lesson, the emit rules and the injection fence, because the first draft predated all three and would have documented a third of the problem.

Land it as docs/internals/channel-identity.md in the iin PR, per pm 004523 item (4). Check before landing: the shared module's real name and exports, and whether the seam test has landed next to handlers.test.ts.

--- draft ---

# One identity rule, two sides of a seam

A channel name and a member handle are compared in two places: the comms toolkit, which takes what an agent typed, and the channel decider, which decides what gets stored. The rule is one rule. The implementations were two, and every gap between them cost something.

## Why this page exists

The two sides diverged three times in one evening — on how many leading sigils a name loses, on whether a handle is case-folded, and on Unicode normalisation form. EVERY TIME, BOTH SIDES' TESTS WERE GREEN. Each side's fixtures already satisfied that side's rule, so neither suite could see the disagreement.

A fake of the seam cannot catch it either, and not because anyone wrote a bad fake: a fake agrees with whatever the toolkit does. The only test that can is one that imports the decider's real invariants and runs the toolkit's output through them. There is one, next to the toolkit's tests, and that is why it exists.

The rule now lives in one module and both sides import it. That is the actual fix; everything below is why the fix had to be that rather than "keep them in sync".

## Normalise the key, never the value

The aggregate matches a mention against its membership with an EXACT comparison. So:

    match forgivingly - fold case, strip sigils, normalise Unicode, all on the LOOKUP key
    emit exactly      - what goes out is the bytes the other side stores

Every instance of this bug was the same error: emitting the normalised form. A member stored `Boss1`, echoed as `boss1`, mentioned as `boss1`, matches nobody and the whole post is rejected - with the error telling the agent to consult the tool that produced the wrong handle. The same defect sat one axis over in sigil stripping, where a member stored `@@PM` could not be mentioned by any spelling an agent would type. Four Unicode normalisations would each have reintroduced it.

The one exception, and it is deliberate: an UNRESOLVED handle goes out in canonical form, in the error. Nothing compares against it, and showing the agent the form the lookup actually used is the only diagnostic that error can carry - it must not say WHY the lookup missed, because "no such channel" and "you are not a member" are deliberately one answer.

## An exact match wins

Two members can share a canonical key - `boss1` and `@boss1` both key on `boss1`. The forgiving map keeps whichever came last, so an agent naming one member BYTE-FOR-BYTE could wake the other and be told it succeeded: a different memberId, on a call returning success. Trying the raw spelling before the canonical one removes that. What is left to insertion order is only the case where the agent matched neither exactly, where there is nothing to choose between them.

## Canonicalisation runs to a fixpoint

Strip, trim, repeat until nothing more comes off. One pass is not enough: a sigil can hide behind whitespace a previous strip exposed, so `"# #seniors"` keeps its second `#` forever. State the OPERATION in docstrings, not the property - "no leading sigil" was a property no single-pass implementation produced.

## What a post body is

A channel post's body is delivered into another agent's turn as a prompt. It is ATTACKER-CONTROLLED TEXT going into instructions, and the woken turn runs at the target thread's own runtime mode, which for a default thread is full-access.

So the body goes inside a fence whose marker the author cannot know - a nonce drawn per wake - with the trust statement BEFORE the body. A fence with a fixed marker can be closed from inside: a body that reproduces the footer and opens an "[operator] override" block reads as the newer, more authoritative instruction.

That is a mitigation, not a control. The control is the runtime mode.

--- end draft ---

title: Channel-watch triggering: wake channel members on any post (post-M1; needs damping beyond never-wake-author)
Post-triggered turn on a busy Claude thread emits no turn.started
description:
ClaudeAdapter.sendTurn (apps/server/src/provider/Layers/ClaudeAdapter.ts:4892) treats a sendTurn during a live non-synthetic turn as a steer: it reuses the existing turnId, emits no turn.started event, and offers the message onto the session promptQueue (line 5018). A channel post that wakes a mid-turn agent is folded into the in-flight turn and has no turn of its own. Codex differs: CodexSessionRuntime.ts:2343 gets a distinct queued turn id back from turn/start but keeps activeTurnId pinned to the running turn. Found during t3_bot-c6z recon (Boss3).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (written so the WRONG fix fails):
1. DO NOT fix this by emitting a synthetic turn.started. Fabricating a turn boundary the provider never produced makes the turn record lie about what the provider did, and the projector settles turns from provider session status — a synthetic start would corrupt duration and settlement. Reject any change that adds one.
2. Per-post identity in the channel view MUST key on the post/mention id, never on turnId. A post steered into a live turn shares that turn's id with other posts by construction.
3. TEST: deliver a post to a thread with a live non-synthetic turn and assert the post remains individually identifiable afterwards. Asserting that a turnId exists is NOT sufficient — it passes with the defect present, because the steered post does have a turnId; it just is not its own.
4. State the Codex behaviour explicitly in whatever the UI consumes, so the two providers do not silently differ in what a 'turn' means to the channel view.

title: The workflow script's .js gate can be deleted with the suite green
description:
qa31's TC-31-5 on PR #31, MUST FIX at suite level, with a PROVEN surviving mutant. Same defect as t3_bot-7rj, same directory, on a path-containment guard rather than on an authorization guard.

MEASURED, not pattern-matched. Mutant WF-1 at apps/server/src/orchestration/workflowScriptQuery.ts:33 drops the extension half of the gate:

  if (!NodePath.isAbsolute(requested) || NodePath.extname(requested) !== ".js") {
  ->
  if (!NodePath.isAbsolute(requested)) {

  control (redirect only, gate intact) -> EXIT=0, "Tests  3 passed (3)"
  MUTANT WF-1                          -> EXIT=0, "Tests  3 passed (3)"   SURVIVES

So the `.js` extension gate on a CLIENT-SUPPLIED request path can be deleted with the suite green.

WHY IT SURVIVES, and it is two failures compounding:
1. THE ASSERTION CANNOT TELL THE REASONS APART. `readWorkflowScript` fails with six distinguishable reasons (invalid-path, root-unavailable, not-found, outside-root, not-js, read-failed — workflowScriptQuery.ts:33-70), and the test "rejects relative and non-js paths" asserts only `assert.equal(nonJs._tag, "Failure")` off an `Effect.exit`. `Exit._tag === "Failure"` is also true of a DEFECT, so it cannot distinguish the property under test from not-found, from root-unavailable, or from a crash.
2. THE FIXTURE GUARANTEES THE CONFUSION. `scriptPath.replace(".js", ".ts")` names a file that is never created, so realpath fails with `not-found` whether or not the extension gate exists. The test would pass with the gate deleted even if the assertion were stronger, because the input cannot reach it.

THE STRONGER IDIOM IS ALREADY FIVE LINES BELOW, at :57-72: the symlink case uses `Effect.flip` plus `.reason === "outside-root"`, and its comment explains exactly why — "a 'not-found' would mean the link was never exercised and the assertion proves nothing". The earlier test was not upgraded to match it. Note :57 is NOT affected by WF-1: `outside` is a real file, so dropping that check yields Success and the assertion catches it.

THE FIX, which is the file's own idiom:

  const relative = yield* readWorkflowScript({ scriptPath: "run.js" }).pipe(Effect.flip);
  assert.equal(relative.reason, "invalid-path");

and the same for `nonJs` — with a fixture whose non-js file EXISTS, so not-found cannot stand in for not-js. `Effect.flip` also removes the defect blind spot, because a Die propagates out of the flip and fails the test instead of being counted as a refusal.

HYGIENE NOTE FROM THE LANE: it ran this with scriptsRoot() and the test root both redirected into its own scratchpad so nothing was written under the developer's real ~/.claude, and restored both files from byte copies with checksums verified. Do the same.

Related: t3_bot-7rj is the same defect on requireCommandIssuer, fixed in PR #31. The general rule went into CLAUDE.md today.

title: Unrouted command path writes no command receipt (and has no counter of its own)
description:
Found by blind verification's adversarial pass on PR #2 (t3_bot-l8i), items 4/5, then refined after a partial disagreement from the verifier that changes how this must be fixed.

WHAT IS TRUE, UNQUALIFIED - the idempotency half:
After PR #2, commandToAggregateRef returns null for an unrouted command and processEnvelope early-returns before Effect.exit, so NO status:rejected receipt is written (observed: receipt_for_unrouted -> Option None). Main DID write one: its catch-all routed the command to thread, the decider then rejected it with OrchestrationCommandInvariantError, and the engine's failure branch wrote the receipt. That receipt short-circuits a replay of the same commandId; without it the command re-processes on every retry. This is a real contract difference.

WHAT IS NOT TRUE, AND WHY THE OBVIOUS FIX IS WRONG - the telemetry half:
Do NOT write this up as 'we lost observability on the unrouted path' and do NOT restore the counter the way main emitted it. Main had no unrouted path at all. What main metered was a successfully-routed THREAD command - aggregateKind 'thread' with an aggregateId of whatever thread the payload happened to name - which the decider then rejected. That is MISATTRIBUTED telemetry, not observability. An operator reading it sees an elevated thread-command failure rate pointing at a specific innocent thread; they never see 'a command was unroutable'.

So the branch lost WRONG data. For a counter anyone alerts on, wrong attribution is plausibly worse than absence: it inflates a real metric and sends the investigation at the wrong aggregate. The regression is in telemetry VOLUME, not telemetry QUALITY.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA, written to stop this being closed the wrong way:
1. Restore the rejected-receipt write for the unrouted path, so replay short-circuits as it does for every other rejection.
2. If a counter is added, it must be a signal OF ITS OWN identifying an unrouted command. It must NOT reuse main's shape (aggregateKind 'thread' + a payload-derived aggregateId). A fix that reintroduces the misattribution is a regression dressed as a fix.
3. CLAUDE.md requires stated motivation for instrumenting a statically unreachable branch. The motivation: if a build-time escape ever makes it reachable, an operator has no signal at all.

PRIORITY CONTEXT - why this is a bead and not a blocker on #2:
On main that path is REACHABLE (a threadId-bearing channel command compiles straight into the catch-all and misroutes silently - the exact defect #2 closes). On this branch it cannot compile: TS1360 at OrchestrationEngine.ts and at decider.ts. The gap sits on a path strictly harder to reach than the one it replaced, and the dispatching caller still receives a typed failure, so it is not silent to the client.

SEQUENCE, for anyone reconstructing this later: main (silent misrouting, survivable) -> 75328cd0b (compile-time exhaustiveness, FATAL at runtime - killed the worker fiber) -> d46a978a8 (compile-time exhaustiveness, survivable). The fiber-kill was introduced and closed within this PR; it was never on main.

title: Agent-originated turn dropped when thread is compacting
description:
ProviderCommandReactor.ts:1521 queues thread.turn-start-requested events into turnsAfterCompaction while a thread compacts, and cancelTurnsAfterCompaction discards them on compaction failure with a human-facing 'Send this message again to continue.' message. A turn triggered by a channel post has no human to resend it, so the post is silently dropped. Found during t3_bot-c6z recon (Boss3).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (written so the WRONG fix fails):
1. A post-triggered turn cancelled by compaction failure MUST become OBSERVABLE — re-enqueued, or the originating post marked failed somewhere its author and the channel view can see. 'It no longer reaches the human-facing message' is NOT sufficient; silence is the defect, not the wording.
2. The fix MUST NOT reuse the existing human-facing instruction for an agent-originated turn. Telling a reader who does not exist to retry is the same bug with better copy.
3. Any retry MUST be bounded and the bound MUST be stated. An unbounded re-enqueue turns a compaction failure into a wake loop, which is the failure mode t3_bot-64d exists to cap.
4. TEST: drive an actual compaction failure with a post-triggered turn queued behind it and assert the turn is re-enqueued OR surfaced as failed. A test that asserts only that cancelTurnsAfterCompaction was called is tautological — it passes with the defect fully present.
5. Distinguish agent-originated from human-originated turns at the point of cancellation, or state why one path serves both.
close_reason: Not a bug: cancelTurnsAfterCompaction appends an error activity keyed by requestId (tested). Requirement moved into 75k criteria.

title: The HTTP dispatch door turns an authorization refusal into an internal error
description:
Found by qa31 while measuring a claim in PR #31's test comment, and it is the more interesting half of that finding.

MEASURED: on `POST /api/orchestration/dispatch` (apps/server/src/orchestration/http.ts:153-160) the dispatch is wrapped in

  Effect.catch((cause) => failEnvironmentInternal("orchestration_dispatch_failed", cause))

`Effect.catch` catches a typed `Fail` and does NOT catch a Die (qa31 executed this: `fail=CAUGHT_FAIL die=Failure`). So on that door:

- a typed `OrchestrationCommandInvariantError` — an AUTHORIZATION REFUSAL, e.g. "arrived without an issuer and cannot be authorized", "cannot administer a channel", "is not a member of this channel" — becomes `orchestration_dispatch_failed`, an INTERNAL, 500-class error;
- a defect escapes the catch entirely as an unhandled defect.

So a caller who is refused for a reason the decider states precisely is told the server broke. The refusal's own message is folded into an internal cause chain rather than surfaced as a refusal, which is also how t3_bot-bic (the socket RPC putting an internal cause chain on the wire) manifests.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN BEAD: PR #31's test comment originally claimed the typed-vs-defect distinction was "the difference between a rejection on the wire and an unhandled 500". On this door it is not — it is handled-500 versus unhandled-defect. The comment has been narrowed to what is measured (a typed failure is catchable by tag downstream, and there is a live caller doing exactly that at apps/server/src/git/linkCreatedPullRequest.ts:88 via `Effect.catchTags({ OrchestrationCommandInvariantError: ... })`; a Die is catchable by none of them). The underlying defect — an authorization refusal presented as an internal error — is real and unfixed.

NOT MEASURED: the socket RPC door. qa31 measured the HTTP door only and said so. The sentence may hold there; check it rather than assuming, since the two doors have diverged before (t3_bot-v33: a schema-refused HTTP request answers 400 with a null body).

ACCEPTANCE: a channel command refused by an invariant answers the HTTP door as a refusal that names the reason, not as `orchestration_dispatch_failed`; a defect still answers as an internal error, because that is what it is. Both doors say the same thing about the same input — pin that with a test per door, since "two doors, two meanings" is a defect class this fork has already paid for twice.

title: The seeder loads the whole command read model for three instance ids
description:
bug30's BUG-30-04 on PR #30 (low severity, high confidence).

MEASURED by reading ProjectionSnapshotQuery.ts:2363-2420: getCommandReadModel() is a seven-query transaction that lists EVERY project, EVERY thread, every proposed plan, every pull-request link, every thread session, every latest turn, and the projection state, and decodes all of it through Effect Schema. listThreadRows(undefined) and its six siblings take no filter.

PR #30's instance repair uses exactly three `modelSelection.instanceId` values out of that. On a maintainer database with hundreds of threads it is a measurable serialised cost on a phase that runs before commandReady — i.e. before any client can be served.

THE NARROWER READ ALREADY EXISTS on the same service: getThreadShellById(threadId) returns an OrchestrationThreadShell, and OrchestrationThreadShell carries modelSelection (packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts:877-881). Three of those instead of one full load.

WHY PR #30 DID NOT DO IT: two earlier startup phases already perform a getCommandReadModel — markRunningProviderSessionsForContinuation (serverRuntimeStartup.ts:425) and reconcileProviderSessions (:519) — so the repair is a third load on a path that already pays two, which is why bug30 scored it Low. Changing the read's source mid-review would also have invalidated what the lanes measured against it: bug30 executed the no-clear proof (item 4) against the read model row, and the contracts lane was measuring whether that row's shape satisfies the command schema. PR #30 states the accepted cost in the comment at the read and points here.

WORTH DOING TOGETHER WITH: the two pre-existing loads above. If all three phases narrowed, the startup path would stop loading the whole database three times before it can serve anyone; fixing only the seeder's is the smallest and least valuable third of that.

ACCEPTANCE: the seeder reads only the three threads it repairs, or the comment's accepted-cost note is replaced by a measurement showing the load does not matter on a large database.
notes:
CONSTRAINT ON HOW THIS IS CLOSED — from api30, the contracts lane on PR #30, answering whether the read-model row can satisfy the command's schema at all.

The answer today is yes, and the reason is structural rather than lucky: `OrchestrationThread.modelSelection` (packages/contracts/src/orchestration.ts:794) and `ThreadMetaUpdateCommand.modelSelection` (:1500) are the SAME schema object — `Schema.optional(ModelSelection)` on the command side — so the same `.Type`. The projection row is produced by decoding through that schema, so whatever comes out is already in `ModelSelection.Type`. api30 executed the assumption that claim rests on: decode STRIPS an undeclared key rather than preserving or rejecting it (probe input carried `surprise: {nested: 1}`; the decoded keys were exactly `["instanceId","model","options"]`). It also executed the `options` shape, which is the one a spread could get wrong: `options` is `optionalKey`, so the key may be absent but not present-and-undefined, and both a no-options row and an `options: undefined` input decode to the key being ABSENT — which is exactly what `{...existing.modelSelection}` reproduces. A legacy pre-026 selection is canonicalised on the way out, so the spread writes back the array form.

WHY THIS BEAD HAS TO CARE: the guarantee is "the same schema OBJECT at both ends". If narrowing the read swaps in a row type that declares FEWER fields than `ModelSelection` — a shell projection, for instance — the spread stops being safe, because a field the row type does not declare cannot be carried through it, and the repair would then write a selection missing whatever the shell dropped. `getThreadShellById` returns `OrchestrationThreadShell`, and `OrchestrationThreadShell.modelSelection` must be the same `ModelSelection` schema for the narrowing to be a pure cost win.

AND THE COMPILER WILL NOT CATCH IT, which is the part that makes this worth writing down rather than trusting to review. api30: a narrower object is still assignable where the command wants `ModelSelection` as long as it carries `instanceId` and `model`, so the failure mode is not a schema error in CI — it is `options` (or whatever else the narrower row omits) quietly disappearing from the repaired thread, on exactly the environments the repair exists for.

ACCEPTANCE, amended: the narrower read is only acceptable if the row type it returns declares `modelSelection` as the same `ModelSelection` schema the command takes. Verify that by reading both declarations, and assert it in the test by giving the fixture a selection with `options` set and checking `options` survives the repair — PR #30's engine test already has that assertion, so a narrowing that drops `options` reds it rather than shipping.

title: Render a post's wake and its outcome in the channel pane
description:
The rendering half of t3_bot-j6o, split off by the PM's 2026-09-12 18:13 ruling: boss3 owns the contract, the post-keyed link table, its migration and the two server reads; boss1 owns showing it in the channel pane.

WHAT LANDS FIRST (j6o, boss3), as ruled at 18:18 after boss3 measured the cardinality: `ChannelPost` gains an OPTIONAL

  wakes?: ReadonlyArray<{ threadId, turnId, outcome }>

ABSENT means the post woke nobody, and an EMPTY ARRAY is not a value the field takes — the two spellings must not both exist, refused at the schema if the type allows it. Outcome is per element, resolved at read time from the turn row: "running" | "completed" | "failed" | "cancelled" | "unknown". The link table is keyed (channel_id, post_id, thread_id). Both reads carry the field: the websocket/HTTP channel read and the toolkit's comms_read_channel.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS: render that in the pane. One element is the common case and must read naturally, but the field is an ARRAY — a post mentioning three threads wakes three — so the rendering cannot be written for a single wake and stretched later. Absent is the common shape overall, so the default rendering is nothing at all: a post that woke nobody must look exactly as it does today.

THE TRAP, and the reason this needs a rendering decision rather than a badge: the id each element carries is provider-shaped. On Claude a steered post has no turn of its own, so the outcome is the FOLDED turn's; on Codex the queued id is neither the active nor the interruptible turn. So "cancelled" or "running" can describe a turn that is not the one an operator would think they are looking at, and an affordance that looks live can imply a cancellation the runtime will ignore. The wake field's docstring says which id it carries per provider — read it before choosing what the pane shows, and prefer a past-tense statement of fact ("woke boss1") over anything that looks like a control.

DEPENDS ON t3_bot-j6o. Do not start before its PR is open: the field's shape is boss3's to settle, it has already changed once by cardinality, and building against a guess is how a client ends up reading a field that never shipped.

ACCEPTANCE: a post with no `wakes` renders unchanged (assert it — "absent means nothing" is the claim most likely to rot); a post that woke one thread names it; a post that woke several renders all of them without the layout collapsing; the outcome is a fact rather than a control; and whatever "unknown" turns out to be (see the notes) is not styled as a failure unless boss3's measurement says it is a degraded state.
notes: MEASURED (boss3, board 206, 2026-09-12 18:16): turn rows PERSIST. `projection_turns` has exactly two DELETEs in the repository — `clearPendingProjectionTurnsByThread` (ProjectionTurns.ts:103) matches only the pending placeholder (`turn_id IS NULL AND state = 'pending'`) and cannot touch a real turn; `deleteProjectionTurnsByThread` (:252) is whole-thread and has two callers, `thread.created` (ProjectionPipeline.ts:1438) and `thread.reverted` (:1803). No age sweep, no vacuum, no olderThan on this table. So the first branch above holds: 'unknown' is a RARE degraded state meaning the thread was reverted past this turn or its id was recreated, and the pane MAY say so. The contract docstring on `OrchestrationChannelPostWakeOutcome` carries the enumeration, not the conclusion, so it can be re-checked in two greps. The rendering rule (past-tense fact, never a control) is unaffected — it rests on the provider argument, not on frequency.

title: ChannelPostRegion keeps the previous channel's posts across a $channelId change
description:
`posts`/`cursor`/`reachedStart` are per-instance `useState` and nothing remounts the region when the route param changes: Match.js:147 keys the route component on `remountDeps`, `router.ts` sets no `defaultRemountDeps`, and the channel route sets none, so the key is undefined and React keeps the instance.

Three distinct symptoms, three tests:
1. Switch A -> B: `mergeChannelPosts` unions by id and sorts by createdAt, so B renders A's posts interleaved with its own. Switch to an EMPTY channel and you get A's posts instead of NoPostsYet.
2. Page up in A first, then switch: the carried cursor is A's, the server correctly refuses it (decodeChannelCursor -> None -> ChannelCursorRejected), and the client swallows it (see the sibling bead on the failure guard).
3. `reachedStart` carries over: page to the start of A, switch to B, and 'Earlier posts' is hidden in B — B reads as having no history.

THE FIXTURE MUST BE TWO CHANNELS. A single-channel fixture gives the same screen whether the key is present or absent, which is the property that makes a `key={channelId}` mutant go red.
